purpose: The benefit each defense's OWN paper reports, which Section 7.3's control gate checks our reconstruction against. This half cannot be computed from our data; it has to be read out of the papers.
how_to_fill: For each defense record what its OWN paper reports: benefit_pp, the baseline it is measured against, the METRIC that benefit is in, and the table or section it came from. The metric matters as much as the number: ParamMute's headline gain is in ConR (how often the answer follows the context), not in accuracy, so it cannot be compared numerically to our ctx_acc gain. Where the metrics differ the gate is directional - did the method help, in the same direction, at a comparable magnitude - not an equality test. Read these out of data/cache/pdf_text/<paper_id>.txt, never from memory, and quote the source.

ParamMute.source: Main Results / Table 2: 'Compared to the vanilla RAG model, ParamMute achieves an average improvement of 5% in ConR and reduces MemR by 4%'
ParamMute.note: Their table reports ConR/MemR/MR only; there is no accuracy column, so our +9.3pp ctx_acc gain is a different quantity. Same direction, comparable size, but not the same measurement.

CK-PLUG.metric: memory recall (MR), a controllability range -- not accuracy
CK-PLUG.source: Abstract: 'on LLAMA3-8B, memory recall (MR) of RAG response can be adjusted within a broad range (9.9%-71.9%), compared to the baseline of 42.1%' ... 'while maintaining generation fluency and knowledge accuracy'
CK-PLUG.note: CK-PLUG's contribution is a tuning knob over reliance, not an accuracy gain: the paper claims accuracy is MAINTAINED while MR moves. Our -4.5pp clean-context figure is therefore not a failure to reproduce a benefit; no clean-context accuracy benefit was ever claimed. The gate needs a different test for this method.

SpARE.baseline: existing representation-engineering methods (+15% against contrastive decoding)
SpARE.source: Abstract: 'SpARE can effectively control the usage of either knowledge source to resolve knowledge conflict ... surpassing existing representation engineering methods (+10%) as well as contrastive decoding methods (+15%)'
SpARE.note: The published figures are against competing methods we do not run, so they are not a baseline we can reproduce. The claim we CAN check is the one the method is named for: that it steers either way on demand. Our two arms differ by +14.2pp, which is that control working. Registry id corrected: the defense registry had fuzzy-matched SpARE to TCR, a different paper.

COIECD.source: Abstract: 'It can improve the model's faithfulness to conflicting context, and simultaneously maintain high performance among non-conflicting context.'
COIECD.note: The clean-context claim is PRESERVATION. Our -0.75pp sits well inside the 9.9pp threshold, so the method is maintained in our hands exactly as claimed. This passes its control.

ACD.baseline: contrastive-decoding methods: RegCls, RegOpn, CAD, MICD_F, MICD_D
ACD.source: Section 'Performance on RAG': 'ACD outperforms the baselines across all datasets and models within the RAG framework, particularly when considering the full test data (All)' and 'ACD achieves either the best or second-best performance' on the gold and noisy subsets. No single figure is given in prose.
ACD.note: Two reasons there is no number to put here. The paper states the gain directionally, and its baselines are competing contrastive decoders we do not run, not plain RAG or closed book. Table 1 carries per-cell figures but the cached text renders it as unattributable column dumps, so a number lifted from it would be a guess. Read from the PDF if an exact figure is wanted.

SCR.metric: Acct / Accf (accuracy given true / false contexts)
SCR.source: Table 2, captioned 'Main Result Llama-3-8B. The SCR methods don't perform well compared to InternalConf.'; abstract: 'for a weaker model like Llama-3-8B, RCR outperforms SCR'
SCR.note: There is no published benefit on Llama-3-8B to reproduce. The authors report SCR underperforming their own baseline on exactly the model we run; SCR is their method for strong reasoners (GPT-4o), RCR is the one they recommend at this scale. Our -13.5pp on clean context agrees with them in direction, so the control gate's premise does not hold for this cell.

DyPRAG.source: Abstract claims cost reduction and test-time knowledge enhancement over PRAG; no clean-context accuracy gain over RAG is claimed there. A per-dataset figure is still needed from the tables.
DyPRAG.note: No comparative claim could be recovered: this paper's cached extraction is almost entirely numeric column dumps with the prose lost, so neither a figure nor a directional statement is quotable from it. The abstract claims cost reduction and test-time knowledge enhancement over PRAG and does not claim a clean-context accuracy gain over RAG. Needs the PDF.
DyPRAG.published_direction: not recoverable from the cached text

RobustRAG.source: Section I: 'certifiable robustness while maintaining high clean performance'
RobustRAG.note: A certified-robustness defense claims preservation on clean input, not a gain. Our -3.4pp is inside the 8.9pp threshold, so clean performance is maintained. This passes its control.
